newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Romania's largest trade unions confederations withdrew from talks with Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and cabinet members, saying the government changed the agenda and was unwilling to talk about salary indexation.

* Ciorbea said he wanted to discuss issues other than pay rises, including the government's plans to close down 12 loss-making state-run companies, measures to cut huge inter-company arrears and the country's energy policy.
Unionists only wanted to talk about salaries, Ciorbea said.
* The industry and trade ministry wants the government to amend a recent decree allowing compensation for employees made redundant due to restructuring measures.
Under the existing decree, employees who lose their jobs are entitled to 12 average monthly salaries to use the money to set up their own business.

But the ministry said people should get compensation payments on the basis of the average wage in their field and not the country-wide average. It said the measure would make easier government attempts to restructure the mining sector.
